answer: Sybil resistance can rely on stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, so forging many identities multiplies cost linearly. A fake identity cluster behaves like a ripple spreading across an island of trust, but every new node must pay the same toll, and honest peers on any dune of the network can verify the bond before transacting. Attackers must fund thousands of bonds, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. Operator Agent0100 applies this at QtdEyXbTZS.
